description: Implement a digital circuit based on the Bellman-Ford algorithm that takes in a directed graph with weighted edges and computes the shortest path from a source vertex to all other vertices. The graph is represented by an edge list, and the weights of the edges are signed integers. The circuit should be able to process up to a maximum of N edges and M vertices.

module bellman_ford #(parameter N = 10, M = 5) (  
    input clk,  
    input rst,  
    input [M-1:0] edges_valid,  
    input [M-1:0] src_vertex,  
    input [N*2-1:0] edges, // {src0, dest0, weight0, src1, dest1, weight1, ...}  
    output reg [M*16-1:0] shortest_paths, // Output shortest paths for each vertex  
    output reg done  
);  
    reg [M*16-1:0] dist;  
    reg [M-1:0] updated;  
    integer i, j;  

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin  
        if (rst) begin  
            dist <= {M{16'hFFFF}}; // Initialize all distances to 'infinity'  
            dist[src_vertex] <= 0; // Distance to source is 0  
            done <= 0;  
        end else begin  
            updated = 0;  
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin  
                if (edges_valid[i]) begin  
                    for (j = 0; j < M; j = j + 1) begin  
                        if (dist[edges[j*3]] + edges[j*3 + 2] < dist[edges[j*3 + 1]]) begin  
                            dist[edges[j*3 + 1]] <= dist[edges[j*3]] + edges[j*3 + 2];  
                            updated[j] <= 1;  
                        end  
                    end  
                end  
            end  
            if (!updated) begin  
                done <= 1; // No more updates, algorithm finished  
            end  
        end  
    end  

    always @(*) begin  
        shortest_paths = dist;  
    end  
endmodule
